posts.title: Rise of the Machines
posts.description: If I had a pound for every Facebook post I’d seen this week complaining about AI slop I’d be a rich man. As a gigging musician who also writes and releases original music, I am surrounded by creative people. As musicians, artists, poets and writers we see the increasingly generic nature of AI generated content. If you have seen one Halloween themed gig or event poster churned out by ChatGPT in the last few weeks, you have seen them all. People are increasingly exhausted by “AI slop” because it prioritizes quantity over quality, flooding the internet with generic, repetitive, and often inaccurate content. This automated filler buries genuine human insight and creativity, making it harder to find authentic perspectives online. Instead of adding value, it creates a frustrating digital landscape where users are forced to sift through endless, soulless text just to find a simple answer. posts.title: Vote for me for General Synod
posts.description: If you know me or have followed me online, you will have heard me talk about the work I have done as a member of General Synod. I am seeking reelection for the next five years and I would be very grateful for your first choice vote if you are clergy in the Diocese of Leeds. Why should you trust me once more as your representative? At the bottom of this post you will find my official election address in which I outline the priorities I see for the national life of the Church of England in the coming five years and the previous experience I bring to the role. I am known for the work that I have done for the last ten years advocating for parishes in low income communities and I include one of the speeches that I gave to synod last year. However, I am not a single issue candidate and in my address you will find priorities of parish finance, clergy wellbeing, mission and evangelism and inclusion. posts.title: Chatting about Estates, Working Class Vocations and Music with Alex Frost
posts.description: I was invited by Alex Frost to come onto his podcast to talk about my love of heavy metal and how I made the transition from a kid in a mining family to priest in the Church of England. I didn’t realise it was a a video until 3/4 of the way in. I would have brushed my hair!
